newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE DOLLAR PARES LOSSES BUT WORST NOT OVER.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE DOLLAR PARES LOSSES BUT WORST NOT OVER.

text.p: The Singapore dollar recovered some poise late on Tuesday after briefly hitting fresh 37-month lows against the U.S. dollar on a perception that local authorities were comfortable with its current weakness.
But dealers said the domestic currency remained susceptible to further declines and was likely to head soon for the 1.53, and even 1.55, to the U.S. dollar levels.
The Singapore dollar was at 1.5050/70 to the U.S. dollar at 0915 GMT after falling through the psychological 1.50 support earlier and heading as low as 1.5140 on stop-loss selling.
Dealers attributed the bulk of the move to comments by a Monetary Authority of Singapore official who told reporters the Singapore dollar's level was appropriate to what was happening in the market.

The official of the de facto central bank said the U.S. dollar had been rising in currency markets and the Singapore dollar had depreciated by about five percent against the U.S. unit since the start of 1997.
"There was some corporate selling of (U.S) dollars near the 1.5140 level, but the market still looks biddish on dollars," a U.S. bank dealer said.
The market shrugged off news that Singapore's manufacturing sector expanded by 3.2 percent year on year in the second quarter of 1997 after three consecutive quarters of decline.
Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Friday the economy was expanding faster than expected and would grow at between six and seven percent in 1997.
"They're supposed to be good figures but now the market is very short of (U.S.) dollars and nobody is looking at fundamentals at the moment," the dealer said.
